intro: Excel to JSON turns an Excel sheet into JSON data ready for a web app, an API, a script or a document database. It is the quick way to bring into code a table someone maintains in Excel: a product catalogue, a price list, translations or a project's configuration.

By default you get a list of objects in which the first row names the keys: each row of the sheet becomes an object such as {"Customer": "Smith", "Amount": 1234.5}. If headers repeat or are empty, keys are numbered (“id_2”, “columna_3”) so none is lost. You can also ask for the rows as they are, as lists of values.

Types are respected: numbers stay numbers (whole numbers without “.0”), logical values are true and false, empty cells are null and dates are written as ISO text (2026-01-15). The calculated values of formulas are used; if a program saved formulas without calculating them, we warn you.

You can convert only the active sheet or all of them, and then the JSON is an object with one entry per sheet. The file is indented, in UTF-8 and with accented letters unescaped. We read the workbook with openpyxl on our server, without running macros, with up to 20 workbooks per batch.
steps: Choose objects or rows and which sheets to convert.

faq.q: What if my table does not start on the first row?
faq.a: Empty rows at the top are skipped and the first row with data gives the keys. If there is a title above the header, delete it before converting or choose “Lists of values” and drop the extra rows.

faq.q: Can I convert a CSV to JSON?
faq.a: Yes, with CSV to JSON, which also detects the file's separator and encoding.

faq.q: Can dates come out as numbers?
faq.a: No: they are always written as ISO text, which almost every language and database understands.
